clue.text: Grow up in Kent with taste for beer!

definitions.text: Grow up in Kent with taste for beer!

parts.words: Grow up in Kent with taste for beer!
parts.note: the climbing flowers that flavour bitter are grown up tall poles in the Kent fields

explanation.surface: A youngster in Kent matures and acquires a liking for ale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grow up' reads as maturing, but it means plants climbing their poles; Kent, a county in south-east England, is the traditional home of the crop that gives beer its bitterness.
explanation.definitionFit: The cone-like flowers of the climbing plant are grown on tall frames in Kent and used to flavour beer.

clue.text: Initially, have no pig pen-a new occurrence, this!

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made into a fresh arrangement
initially points to the opening letters of the words have and no

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the letters of pen and a

explanation.surface: A farmer without a sty for the pig: what a novel state of affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' takes H and N from 'have no'; 'new' shuffles them with PIGPENA.
explanation.definitionFit: An event or something that takes place is called an occurrence, a synonym.

clue.text: Be late in honouring bills? It's a spiteful thing to do

definitions.meaning: humorously, to pay accounts that have long been owing

definitions.text: It's a spiteful thing to do
definitions.meaning: to take revenge for past grievances

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means taking revenge for old wrongs, while literally it is paying off long-standing debts.

clue.text: Distinctly said it wasn't like this

definitions.text: Distinctly said it wasn't like this

parts.words: Distinctly said it wasn't like this
parts.note: something said indistinctly, under the breath, is the opposite of something said distinctly

explanation.surface: Someone firmly insisted that events did not happen this way.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a denial, but 'it wasn't like this' means the manner of speaking was not distinct.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking low and indistinctly is the opposite of speaking distinctly, so this is the word for unclear speech.

clue.text: Example of one Oklahoma show

definitions.meaning: Oklahoma! is a famous Rodgers and Hammerstein stage work with songs
a stage production with songs and dancing

explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma! is a classic of the song-and-dance stage genre, and such a production is a show.

clue.text: Found around many a head wound!

definitions.text: Found around many a head wound!

parts.words: Found around many a head wound!
parts.note: wound here is the past tense of wind: lengths of cloth wrapped round the head

explanation.surface: Bandages are commonly seen around injuries to the scalp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' reads as an injury but is the past of 'wind': cloth wrapped round the head.
explanation.definitionFit: These are long cloths wrapped around the head as headwear, worn by many Sikhs and others.

clue.text: Loves three to get people in such an awkward situation

definitions.text: Loves three to get people in such an awkward situation

parts.words: Loves three to get people in such an awkward situation
parts.note: a love affair among three people, one of whom is shut out, is a famously awkward state of affairs

explanation.surface: A love of threesomes gets people into embarrassing scrapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loves three' reads as a liking for the number, but it means three people tangled in love.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a romantic situation involving three people, typically a couple and a lover.

clue.text: Maybe 'shoots out for a game

definitions.meaning: moves suddenly and swiftly, as a tongue or a lizard does
the pub sport of throwing small missiles at a board

explanation.surface: Perhaps shooting out is a way to play a game.
explanation.definitionFit: To dart is to move suddenly; the plural is also the name of the pub game played with small feathered missiles.

clue.text: Perhaps makes fearless people guard one who does!

definitions.text: Perhaps makes fearless people guard one who does!

parts.words: Perhaps makes fearless people guard one who does!
parts.note: someone who shields people makes them unafraid, and a bodyguard does exactly this

explanation.surface: A tough guy perhaps makes brave people stand watch over himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on the sense of keeping safe: whoever shields someone makes them fearless, and a guard is one who does it.
explanation.definitionFit: To guard or shield someone, keeping them safe from harm, is the meaning.

clue.text: Took jet-propelled passengers in space

parts.note: the de Havilland airliner of that name was the first jet passenger plane, and the same word names a body travelling through space

explanation.surface: A spacecraft carried passengers by jet propulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: The de Havilland Comet, a British plane of the 1950s, was the first jet airliner; the word also names an icy body in space.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both the first jet airliner and an icy celestial body with a tail that travels through space.

clue.text: Smoking jacket for the cannabis party?

definitions.text: Smoking jacket for the cannabis party?

parts.words: Smoking jacket for the cannabis party?
parts.note: the word names both a short double-breasted jacket and a marijuana cigarette

explanation.surface: What should one wear to a gathering where cannabis is smoked?
explanation.walkthrough: A smoking jacket is a lounging garment, but here the word is both a short thick jacket worn by sailors and a cannabis cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a thick double-breasted sailor's jacket and a hand-rolled cannabis cigarette.

clue.text: Assemble many to hide this badge

indicators.note: to hide signals that the answer lies concealed within the words assemble many

explanation.surface: A crowd is gathered to conceal a badge.
explanation.definitionFit: A badge is a symbolic device worn or displayed, a synonym.

clue.text: Programmes on these bodies of water

definitions.meaning: straits or narrow seas, like the one between England and France

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both broadcasting stations and narrow stretches of sea between land masses.

clue.text: Won't stop living like a god!

definitions.text: Won't stop living like a god!

parts.words: Won't stop living like a god!
parts.note: a being that never dies, as the gods of myth were said to be

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to give up a lavish lifestyle fit for a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Living like a god' suggests luxury, but it means literally never dying.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that never dies, as gods are thought to live forever, is deathless.

clue.text: When this puzzle is sent in, it may receive a prize

definitions.text: When this puzzle is sent in, it may receive a prize

parts.words: When this puzzle is sent in, it may receive a prize
parts.note: a completed competition crossword may win the sender a prize

explanation.surface: Entries for this crossword competition might win an award.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue speaks of the very puzzle in hand: only a completed, worked-out grid can win the prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzle that has been worked out completely is the kind you send in for the prize draw.

clue.text: Gets the group going, in many different ways

definitions.text: Gets the group going, in many different ways

parts.words: Gets the group going, in many different ways
parts.note: breaking up a crowd sends its members off in all directions

explanation.surface: A leader rouses the band with many different approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets the group going' sounds like motivating them, but it means sending them away in all directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Scattering a crowd or breaking it up so its members go off in various directions is the sense.

clue.text: Ranks and classes in America

definitions.meaning: levels or positions in a hierarchy
in the US, school years or forms are called by this word

explanation.definitionFit: The word means levels of rank, and in American schools it names the year groups pupils are in.

clue.text: Give a quarter to a bank manager, for instance that's not a gross figure!

indicators.note: give to means add one piece in front of the next

parts.note: S, south, is one of the four quarters of the compass
a bank manager is an example of someone who lends money

explanation.surface: Tipping a bank manager twenty-five cents hardly makes for a large sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gross figure' suggests a pre-tax amount, but it means a fat body; 'quarter' is a compass point, not a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin, slim body is the opposite of a fat or gross figure.

clue.text: Rare site rebuilt for blood supplies

indicators.note: rebuilt means the letters of rare and site are put together in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An unusual location is reconstructed to house a blood bank.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the vessels that carry blood from the heart, so they supply blood to the body.

clue.text: Takes it for granted it's me in The States, after a ship

indicators.note: after places the following piece behind the earlier ones

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the standard prefix for a ship

indicators.note: in places the word me inside the letters for the States

parts.note: US is short for the United States
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone presumes they are the one in America after a vessel arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' is only a link; 'The States' as the US is the clue's American flavour, and the inner piece makes UMES.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something for granted is to suppose it true without proof, which is to presume.

clue.text: Big man, an artist I abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned means the letter I is dropped from the painter's name

parts.note: Titian was the great Venetian Renaissance painter

explanation.surface: A painter is deserted by a large fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' drops the letter I from TITIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the giants who preceded the Olympian gods give their name to any very big or important person.

clue.text: Runs home to them, providing food

definitions.text: Runs home to them, providing food

parts.words: Runs home to them, providing food
parts.note: a run is an enclosure for keeping poultry, which supply eggs and meat

explanation.surface: Someone hurries home to the family, bringing something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' reads as hurrying, but a run is a pen for poultry, and the birds kept there provide food.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic fowl kept in runs are a source of eggs and meat, which is food.

clue.text: First file it, then get out the gold, etc — you hope!

definitions.text: First file it, then get out the gold, etc — you hope!

parts.words: First file it, then get out the gold, etc — you hope!
parts.note: a prospector registers a stake on land before mining it, hoping to find gold

explanation.surface: A prospector's plan: do the paperwork, then dig out the riches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'File it' sounds like office paperwork, but a prospector stakes and registers a plot before mining it.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospector stakes a plot of land, registering a right to mine it, and this word names that right.

clue.text: A state of medium or partial unconsciousness

definitions.meaning: the condition a spiritualist medium enters when contacting the dead

explanation.definitionFit: The word names the hypnotic half-conscious state, which mediums claim to enter at seances.

clue.text: Read? Do — about being very highly thought of!

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of read and do are moved around

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to read, then a plea to get on with it, for a well-regarded book.
explanation.definitionFit: Something loved and worshipped is regarded very highly indeed.

clue.text: They don't mind their own business

definitions.text: They don't mind their own business

parts.words: They don't mind their own business
parts.note: to mind a business is to run it, and these people run businesses owned by others

explanation.surface: Nosy people meddle in other people's affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom suggests busybodies, but 'mind' means run: these people run firms owned by other people.
explanation.definitionFit: These people run or direct a business on behalf of its owners.

clue.text: As it were, sizes up old dances

definitions.meaning: a stately dance of earlier centuries went by this name

explanation.definitionFit: The word means takes dimensions, and was also the name for grave, stately dances of Tudor times.

clue.text: Finishes with dead dog, too

parts.note: dead ___ and dog ___ are both phrases using the word for finishes: a blind alley and a cigarette butt

explanation.surface: Someone finally gets rid of a deceased pet as well.
explanation.walkthrough: A dead end is a blind alley and a dog end is British slang for a cigarette butt.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means conclusions or finishes, and combines with dead and dog in common phrases.
